synonyms: Lonicera dumosa (historical synonym; concept review if encountered)

project_inclusion.source_count: see Master Plant Pool authoritative row
project_inclusion.range_basis: Native to Texas at state level under Kew/POWO and regional floras. BONAP/NAPA 3-target-county threshold not certified in this pass; no native-only county tally.

look_here_first: Usually an arching shrub or scrambling vine. Start at a TERMINAL flowering shoot: pale 2-lipped relatively short flowers, usually 17–20 mm, with connate/perfoliate terminal floral bracts. A leaf pair fused beneath the inflorescence does NOT prove coral honeysuckle; both share it.

morphology_keys.habit: Shrubby, arching or scrambling growth; leafy stems opposite, simple, usually short-petiolate; upper fused terminal bracts possible.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Opposite simple leaves with entire to near-entire margins; petiole lengths and fused terminal bracts vary by species.
morphology_keys.flower: Cream or white short clearly two-lipped corollas usually about 17–19.5 mm long in condensed terminal inflorescences; petals fused into corolla; calyx sits above inferior ovary.
morphology_keys.fruit: Red-orange to scarlet berries about 6.5–10 mm; fruit color does not separate from coral honeysuckle.
diagnostic_sequence: Follow the flower stalk to determine AXILLARY paired flowers versus TERMINAL whorls.
Check one lateral flower: short two-lipped (~17–20 mm) / long tubular (~38–48 mm) / long strongly two-lipped (~45–57 mm).
Examine whether fused terminal bracts occur; do NOT use fused bracts alone for native pair.
If berries are ripe, note red-or-orange vs black—but berries are supporting evidence.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus L. sempervirens, short strongly two-lipped cream flowers (~17–20 mm) versus the long (~38–48 mm) mostly tubular coral trumpet with short lobes. Both can show a fused upper pair. Versus L. japonica, albiflora flowering clusters are terminal and berries red, while japonica has axillary flower pairs and black berries.
